text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition leaders Michael Kijana Wamalwa and Mwai Kibaki declare their willingness to sacrifice their ambition for presidency in favour of a single presidential candidate.
- President Daniel arap Moi says imported sugar will be taxed heavily to protect the local sugar industry from collapse.
- A public rally convened by constitutional reform lobbyists will be held on Saturday at Nairobi's Kamukunji grounds.
- Police and members of the public recover three missing bodies buried alive this week in a landslide.
- President Moi orders a review of minimum wages in the country.
- The Central Organisation of Trade Unions calls for the review of outdated labour laws.
- President Moi orders the splitting of Nairobi province into administrative boroughs to ease the management of basic services.
-The government bans Kenyans from seeking employment in Saudi Arabia.
- A major political showdown between supporters and opponents of Simeon Nyachae is averted when the president dismisses a call for fresh ruling party elections in Kisii district.
